turns.content: I've been working from home for years now. I live alone. I go days without speaking to anyone.
Days of silence and isolation — that's a significant deficit of human connection. Have you found ways to build contact into your routine?
I try. I have a standing call with a friend on Sundays. But she has a family now and I can hear how distracted she is. I don't want to bother her.
Feeling like a burden to the people in your life can make isolation self-reinforcing. How long has it been this way?
Years, honestly. It's just got more extreme. I used to care. Now I'm not sure I do. I've started to think I could disappear and no one would really notice.
That thought — that you could disappear and no one would notice — is something I don't want to let pass. What do you mean by disappear?
Die, I suppose. I've thought about it more seriously lately. Not dramatically, just quietly. Like turning off a light no one needs.
You deserve to be noticed and to matter. Are you safe right now?
For now. But the thought is getting louder. I'm not sure what to do with it.
